title: Ear Pain
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute ear pain, pulling at ear, fever, and recent URI. Otoscopy reveals a bulging, erythematous, non-mobile tympanic membrane with loss of landmarks. AOM is the most common bacterial infection in children. Common organisms: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis. Diagnosis: acute onset + middle ear effusion (bulging TM, impaired mobility, otorrhea) + signs of inflammation (erythema, otalgia). Treatment: watchful waiting for 48-72h if >6mo, unilateral, non-severe. If <6mo, bilateral, or severe: amoxicillin 80-90mg/kg/day x 10d (first-line). Amoxicillin-clavulanate if recent amoxicillin use or treatment failure. NO decongestants or antihistamines — not effective. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) for prevention.
